public_rationale: The speaker links the token caps and cost complaints to a claim that 'AI’s revenue growth is slowing'. Results for April–June 2026, the quarter of the post, show the opposite at the main sellers. Microsoft's Azure revenue grew 43% year over year, up from 40% the quarter before. Anthropic's revenue rose from $4.73 billion to $11.56 billion, up 144% on Q1. That is faster than Q1's roughly 132% rise over Q4 2025. The caps he describes may be real, but the growth they were meant to signal as slowing actually sped up.
limitations: 'Signs' is partly interpretive, and the speaker gave no metric.
OpenAI's growth was not checked from primary data.
Azure growth includes non-AI cloud services and compute sold to Anthropic and OpenAI.

our_interpretation: The speaker ties his 'signs' (token caps and cost complaints) to the claim that 'AI’s revenue growth is slowing'. The plain reading tested is whether commercial AI revenue growth was slowing around the post date.
The period is Q2 2026 (April–June), the quarter containing the June 8 post. It is the first full period whose results show whether the signs he cites matched a slowdown.

Growth is judged by the year-over-year or quarter-over-quarter growth rate at the main commercial AI sellers the speaker himself focuses on (Anthropic, and Microsoft's Azure, which sells AI compute and models). No single month is used.
criteria.support_condition: Q2 2026 revenue growth at the leading AI sellers slows compared with Q1 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Q2 2026 revenue growth at the leading AI sellers holds steady or speeds up compared with Q1 2026.
